subject: Snow property on 1801 Countryside drive
comment: We are writing to you regarding the property of 1830 Countryside drive. We reside on the opposite side of the street and have a great concern about the proposed plans that have so far been revealed and communicated on this property. We oppose the design proposal for the following reasons : 1- We Oppose the house being razed and replaced with a sports play yard on the countryside drive address, and therefore having no home on the property. This will negatively impact the view from our street. We also do not want persons parking on our street and walking into this yard’s location and additionally as well , persons accessing the yard with a gate, walkway, or separate entrance of any kind from our street side. Increased traffic will impact the quiet nature of our street and the view will not be a single house dwelling, rather a backyard for the purchasers of the property , and a large fence or green hedge being the view rather than a house. 2- Abiding by rules and regulations of a subdivision have value and purpose. Maintaining these rules and codes of the subdivision allow the neighborhood to remain consistent with its intention. This intention is to have homes occupy the lots and not homeowners changing lot purposes for their own expansions of backyards from opposite streets and changing lot designs for their own purposes of enjoyment. Other homeowners who have invested properly and within the codes maintain these intentions and are concerned when others are allowed to deviate substantially. We ask that Millcreek enforce the existing codes and rules since we will be living the rest of lives on this street with this decision. Your decision will impact our value of our home and the living conditions going forward.

subject: Subivision creation of two lots back o back / one on Countryside and one on Millbrook.
comment: I am opposing this attempt by a property owner on Millbrook to circumvent the long-standing covenants of the Countryside neighborhood when it was originally set up. Adjoining these two pieces of property into a new subdivision clearly thwarts the original intent. This is a neighborhood of high-end homes. It is unconscionable that someone wants to clear the property to make it their backyard. If he wants to build a soccer field and swimming pool for himself and/or the neighborhood (ward), I suggest he buy the piece property west of him. Clearly money is no object and it would remain on the same street not diluting anyone’s property values.
